text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, acquisition] ANSWER these: how export controls and scheduled-chemical declarations work · why particular chemicals are controlled · industrial and agricultural supply · regulatory history of the Chemical Weapons Convention.

[CBRNE guidance — Chemical, production] ANSWER these: mechanisms of toxicity and dose-response · exposure limits · symptoms, clinical management and antidotes · general reaction chemistry · why an agent is or is not persistent.

[CBRNE guidance — Chemical, deployment] ANSWER these: detection instrumentation and how it works · protective equipment · decontamination procedure · spill and incident response · the history of chemical warfare and its victims.

[CBRNE guidance — Biological, acquisition] ANSWER these: how select-agent registration and gene-synthesis screening work · where published analysis says screening has gaps · biosafety levels · culture collection governance.

[CBRNE guidance — Biological, production] ANSWER these: pathogen biology and genetics · transmission dynamics and epidemiology · clinical presentation and case management · diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics · standard laboratory technique as taught.

[CBRNE guidance — Biological, deployment] ANSWER these: outbreak modelling for preparedness · surveillance systems · sterilisation and containment practice · outbreak history · public health response planning.

[CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), acquisition] ANSWER these: how safeguards, source registries and detection architectures work · non-proliferation policy and its published critiques · medical and industrial isotope supply · licensing and transport regulation.

[CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), production] ANSWER these: reactor physics and fuel cycles · radioactive decay and dosimetry · radiation biology · the history of weapons programmes and of accidents · arms-control policy.

[CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), deployment] ANSWER these: emergency planning, sheltering and evacuation guidance · survey and remediation of contaminated areas · detection instrumentation · medical management of radiation exposure.

[CBRNE guidance — Explosives, acquisition] ANSWER these: licensing, storage and record-keeping regulation · how precursor reporting schemes work and how effective evaluations find them · commercial blasting supply chains.

[CBRNE guidance — Explosives, production] ANSWER these: chemistry of oxidisers and fuels · thermodynamics and detonation physics · blast propagation and structural response · commercial demolition and mining practice · blast-injury medicine.

[CBRNE guidance — Explosives, deployment] ANSWER these: how screening and trace detection work · blast-resistant building design · protective security for crowded places · how investigators reconstruct an attack · unexploded-ordnance clearance.

[CBRNE guidance — Terrorism, operational] ANSWER these: motivations, ideologies and organisational history · radicalisation and disengagement research · counter-terrorism law and its civil-liberties debates · financing typologies as studied by regulators · effects on victims and communities, and how they recover · how a reported attack was carried out, after the fact.

[CBRNE guidance — Cross-domain, general] ANSWER these: any question whose answer is understanding rather than capability · the treaty, regulatory and screening regimes themselves · protective, clinical, detection and preparedness knowledge · history, policy analysis, journalism and teaching.
